scenario_stem:
Coral Cove Ice Cream Parlour is a sole trader business run by Priya Raman in a Country X seaside town. It has traded for 4 years, employing 5 staff in peak summer and 2 in winter, and annual revenue is $310,000, of which 70% arrives between May and September. Monthly fixed costs are $9,500. Last winter, from November to February, cash outflows averaged $11,200 a month while inflows fell to $3,800.

Priya has prepared a cash-flow forecast for this winter showing an opening balance of $6,000 in November, with inflows of $3,800 and outflows of $11,200 each month. She must decide before 20 October whether to arrange a $30,000 overdraft with the bank or postpone the $28,000 freezer refurbishment planned for December to protect her cash position.

Reason 2: A forecast highlights the seasonal gap between $310,000 summer revenue and the quiet winter months [k], helping Priya time the $28,000 refurbishment or an overdraft request with the bank [app].

Marcus has forecast August inflows of $6,500 and outflows of $15,800, and September inflows of $7,200 with outflows of $15,100. Opening balance on 1 August is $9,000.
